Money & Rules

Model Book
Review

Summary

Matilda is an extraordinary little girl who loves books and is extremely intelligent. However, her parents do not appreciate her at all — they call her stupid and completely ignore her. At school, she meets a kind teacher called Miss Honey, who immediately recognizes Matilda's genius. But the headmistress, Miss Trunchbull, is a horrible tyrant who terrorizes children and teachers alike.

One day, Matilda discovers she has a magical power: she can move objects with her mind. She decides to use this extraordinary gift to help Miss Honey and to stand up to Miss Trunchbull once and for all.

Recommendation

I strongly recommend this book to anyone who has ever felt misunderstood or underestimated. It is perfect for readers aged 9–13 who love magical adventures and strong, independent characters. If you enjoyed the Harry Potter series, you will almost certainly love Matilda too.

Personal
comment

I really enjoyed this book because it shows that intelligence and kindness are more powerful than cruelty and ignorance. I particularly love how Matilda uses both her brain and her telekinesis to solve problems — she is a character you cannot help but admire. The story is funny and exciting, but it also has a deeper message: every child deserves love, encouragement, and support.

However, I think the descriptions of Matilda's parents are somewhat exaggerated — they seem almost too horrible to be believable. But perhaps that is precisely part of Roald Dahl's genius: by making the adults ridiculously bad, he makes Matilda's strength shine even brighter.

Matilda

PROTAGONIST

A small, clever girl with big brown eyes and dark hair. She loves reading and is brave and kind. Despite being treated badly at home, she never gives up.

Miss Honey

 

Matilda's teacher. She is gentle, patient, and caring. She becomes an incredibly important figure in Matilda's life.

Miss Trunchbull

ANTAGONIST

The headmistress of Crunchem Hall. She is huge, aggressive, and cruel to children and staff alike. She is the main villain of the story.

Mr. & Mrs. Wormwood

SECONDARY CHARACTERS

Matilda's parents. They are selfish, ignorant, and completely uninterested in their daughter. They value money over intelligence and kindness.

2.4 Correct the rules
  • The pronoun for the person talking is “i”.
  • We use “you” only for one person.
  • We use “he” for a girl.
  • “They” can only refer to a group of only boys or men.
  • The pronoun for pets is “it”.
  • If we don't know the gender of the person we are talking about, we use “she”.
  • If we respect a person, we use “she” as their pronoun.

🧱 Scaffolding · cards

Bullshit! 🃏

Everybody has some cards with facts. Are they true for you… or are you lying?

  1. Your turn: say one or two of your facts and put the cards on the floor, face down.
  2. Do you think it's a lie? Shout “Bullshit!” and say the sentence in the negative: “You aren't afraid of spiders!”
  3. The cards on the floor: who takes them can play them the opposite way, from positive to negative (or from negative to positive).
  4. The winner is the first player with no cards!

🔄 The opposite form

I am➜I am not · I'm not
he / she / it is➜he / she / it is not · isn't
we / you / they are➜we / you / they are not · aren't
there is · there are➜there isn't · there aren't
  1. I am an only child. ➜ I am not an only child.
  2. My desk is tidy right now. ➜ My desk isn't tidy right now.
  3. I am not a morning person. ➜ I am a morning person. (take away not!)
  4. There isn't a garden at my house. ➜ There is a garden at my house.

Useful language

Bullshit!You aren't… · He isn't…That's true! · That's a lie!It's my turn.Take the cards!I have no cards. I win!

🧱 Scaffolding · lie or truth? · to be

Lie or truth? 🤥

Some cards are perfect for lying: nobody can check them! Others… we know the truth.

🤥 You can lie: nobody can check!

  • I am afraid of spiders.
  • I am afraid of the dark.
  • I am not a morning person.
  • My best friend is in this class.
  • I am hungry right now.
  • I am bored in this lesson.
  • I am the youngest in my family.
  • My room is always messy.
  • I am nervous when I speak in front of the class.

👀 You can't lie: we can check!

  • I am an only child.
  • My mom is younger than 40.
  • I am taller than my mom.
  • I am shorter than my dad.
  • My dad is taller than 1.80 m.
  • My backpack is very heavy today.
  • My desk is tidy right now.
  • My phone is dead right now.
  • My hair is longer than it was last year.
  • I am wearing something red today.
  • I am left-handed.

We know your family, we can see your parents, your desk, your backpack, your clothes… and your hand when you write!

Lie or truth? 🤥

The same with the present simple cards: what can you lie about?

🤥 You can lie: nobody can check!

  • I eat breakfast every morning.
  • I play a musical instrument.
  • I watch more than 2 hours of TV a day.
  • I like horror movies.
  • I read books for fun.
  • I drink coffee.
  • I hate Mondays.
  • I share a bedroom with someone.
  • I forget things very easily.
  • I play football at least once a week.
  • I never eat vegetables.
  • I go to bed after midnight on weekends.
  • I always wash the dishes at home.
  • My mom cooks dinner every night.
  • I cry when I watch sad movies.

mythology

LITERATURE · 1

Prometheus is a Titan, not a god. He is very clever and he is a friend of humans. His gift to humanity is fire. He is not selfish, he is brave and generous. But when Zeus finds out that Prometheus has stolen the fire, he is not happy. His punishment is terrible: Prometheus is chained to a rock. Every day, an eagle is there. Its job is horrible: it eats Prometheus's immortal liver every day.

Zeus is powerful but he is not kind - not to Prometheus.

Greek mythology

ERSEPHONE

The story

Persephone is the daughter of Demeter, the goddess of plants and nature. She is young, happy, and free. Her home is a sunny meadow full of flowers.

One day, Hades, king of the Underworld (also called “Hades” – very original), looks up, sees Persephone, and thinks: “Wow, I want her.”

So he jumps in his black chariot and goes to her: “Hey little girl, do you want to come to my dark world?” Of course she says “No”... but he takes her anyway.

1.3Match each word to its definition.

1.4Complete with the correct possessive adjective

  1. Demeter is the goddess of nature. Persephone is daughter.
  2. Persephone is young and happy. home is a sunny meadow.
  3. Persephone sees many flowers in the meadow. Each color has color.
  4. Hades drives a black chariot. chariot is very fast.
  5. Persephone and Demeter love each other. relationship is very sweet.
  6. "I am Hades," says the god. "The Underworld is home."
  7. Demeter talks to Persephone. "I am mother, listen to me!"
  8. Demeter and Persephone live together. home is beautiful.

In the Underworld, everything is dark and sad. But Persephone is not boring as Hades, so she starts to decorate. She adds some flowers and style. Suddenly, the Underworld looks almost... cozy.

Meanwhile, on Earth, Demeter is super sad. Her daughter is gone! And when Demeter is sad, all the plants die, and everything freezes. 🥶 Nobody even knows what “winter” is yet. But now it is winter every day, and life is terrible.

Zeus, king of the gods, is angry: “Demeter, why is everything cold or dead?” Demeter complains that her sweet daughter is in Hell.

So Zeus goes to the Underworld with one clear rule: “Give Persephone back. And do not let her eat anything here — if she eats food in the Underworld, she must stay.” Hades: “Sure, bro.” But the second Zeus leaves, Hades asks: “Are you hungry, Persephone?” She is. The only food available is... POMEGRANATES!” (another reason the underworld is awesome and Hades should stop complaining.) Hades gives her the seeds — one by one. Six in total.

1.5Complete with is or his

  1. Hades the king of the Underworld.
  2. The Underworld dark and sad.
  3. Hades decorates kingdom with Persephone.
  4. Demeter misses daughter.
  5. Zeus asks, "Why everything cold?"
  6. Hades gives Persephone pomegranate seeds.
  7. Zeus visits Hades in dark kingdom.

Until Demeter arrives: “Daughter, come home!” Hades is firm: “She ate my food. Rules are rules. She stays.” Zeus steps in. He is tired of the argument, and of the cold. His decision is a compromise:

“She ate six seeds. So: six months with Hades in the Underworld, and six months with Demeter on Earth.”

Demeter agrees, but her warning is clear: “When she is gone, I freeze everything!”

And that is why we have seasons. 🌸 ❄️ When Persephone is with her mother, the world is warm and green. When she is in the Underworld, her mother is heartbroken — and the earth is cold.

Greek mythology

ERSEPHONE

The play

Persephone: What a perfect day! Flowers, sunshine… I love it!

Demeter: Enjoy the flowers, dear, but stay close. Gods are not always safe.

Hades (peeking in): Wow! Who is that beautiful girl?

(rolls in with chariot): Hello! I am Hades, king of the Underworld. Free ride? Dark style, five stars.

Persephone: Thanks, but I’m fine here…

(Hades grabs her and “whooshes” offstage).

Demeter: Persephone? PER-SE-PHO-NE?!

Persephone: Mom! Come get me!

Hades: Don’t worry, it’s just… a short trip!

Hades: Welcome to the Underworld!

Persephone: Wow… it’s very dark. Like a sad basement.

Hades: Yeah… I am the king of darkness. My job is to look sad.

Persephone: Challenge accepted. Step one: open the curtains.

Hades: Curtains? We only have eternal night.

Persephone: Then paper stars! Throw pillows! A plant!

Hades: A plant? In my dark kingdom?

Persephone: Yes! Now it looks cozy, almost like home!

Hades: Ugh… fine. One pillow. Black pillow!

Zeus (alone on a cloud): Why is the world frozen? For days! Olive trees are ice, beaches are closed, even my thunder is cold!

This is not okay. I must go down. (Zeus descends to Demeter.)

Demeter, why is there endless winter?

Demeter: My daughter is gone. Hades took Persephone! Without her, the world is empty.

Zeus: Mmmh… I understand. But the old rule says that if she eats food in the Underworld, she must stay there.

I will go to Hades. Don’t worry.

Demeter: Do it! No sunshine until my daughter is back!

Zeus: Hades, remember: no food for Persephone. If she eats, she stays.

Hades (innocent): Of course, big brother.

(Zeus exits.)

Persephone: Hades, sweety, I am hungry, I haven’t eaten for months.

Hades: Snack time! Pomegranate seeds. Red, sweet, totally normal. Here… (Mimes 6 seeds.)

Demeter (storms in): My child! Come home!

Hades: No! She ate my food. Rules are rules. She stays.

Persephone: I didn’t know the rule! I was hungry…

Zeus (returns): Stop! We need peace. Not eternal winter.

Decision: She only ate six seeds, so six months with Hades, six months with Demeter.

Demeter: Fine. But when she is gone, I will make winter.

Hades: Fine. I will clean before she comes back.

Persephone: Don’t ruin my decorations, Hades!

Demeter: When she returns, the flowers and fields will bloom.

Zeus: Six months of sun, six of winter. Good enough!

Common mistakes

Can you spot them before you make them?

Anna loves his dog.

Anna loves her dog.

The owner decides: Anna = she → her.

The my phone is new.

My phone is new.

No “the” before my, your, his, her…

The dog’s are in the garden.

The dogs are in the garden.

A plural is not a possession: no apostrophe.

The car of my father is new.

My father’s car is new.

For people, use ’s, not “of”.

It’s tail is long.

Its tail is long.

its = possessive · it’s = it is

This is mine book.

This is my book.

my + noun · mine stands alone: “It’s mine.”

1.8 Who or what do these words refer to?

  1. "They" called me nymph.
  2. "She" caught my father's eye.
  3. "He" came to visit the halls of her father.
  4. "She is yours if you want her."

First page.

CIRCE- Madeline Miller

When I was born, the name for what I was did not exist. They called me nymph, assuming I would be like my mother and aunts and thousand cousins. Our powers were modest, we spoke to fish and cured flowers.

The word nymph, in our language means not just goddess, but bride. My mother was one of them, guardian of fountains and streams.

She caught my father's eye when he came to visit the halls of her own father, Oceanos. Helios and Oceanos were often at each other's tables in those days. They were cousins, and equal in age. They were both Titans, and preferred each other's company to those new-squeaking gods upon Olympus who had not seen the making of the world. When he noticed my mother, “Who is that?” my father said to Oceanos.

Oceanos had many golden-eyed grandchildren from my father already, and was glad to think of more. “My daughter Perse. She is yours if you want her.”

“It is marriage,” she said to him, “or nothing. And if it is marriage, be sure: you may have what girls you like in the field, but you will bring none home, for only I will hold sway in your halls.” Conditions, constraint. These were novelties to my father, and gods love nothing more than novelty.

A2 Two ways to say it: both are correct!

with DO the way we use in class

I / you / we / they have a dog.

He / she / it has a long tail.

A snake doesn’t have legs.

Do you have a pet?

Yes, I do. · No, I don’t.

Does a bat have wings?

Yes, it does. · No, it doesn’t.

=

with GOT very British

I / you / we / they have got a dog. (I’ve got)

He / she / it has got a long tail. (it’s got)

A snake hasn’t got legs.

Have you got a pet?

Yes, I have. · No, I haven’t.

Has a bat got wings?

Yes, it has. · No, it hasn’t.

Same meaning. In British English you hear have got a lot (songs, films, British people), so you must understand it. Choose one way, but don’t mix them.

Careful! Have got is only for possession. For actions (have breakfast, have a shower) use DO: I don’t have breakfast, not I haven’t got breakfast.

The three ’s

Same shape, three different roles!

’s

after it: an adjective, a noun with a/an, an -ing verb, a place

🕵️ The detective test

4.20Read about Leo’s day. Then click every verb that ends in -s, -es or -ies.

Leo’s day Leo is twelve. He lives in Bologna.

Leo lives with his mom, his dad and his dog, Pepper. On school days he wakes up at seven o’clock. First, he takes Pepper for a short walk. Then he has a quick shower, gets dressed and has breakfast with his dad at twenty-five past seven: he always has milk and cereal. He catches the bus at quarter to eight. School starts at eight o’clock and finishes at half past one. Leo has lunch at home with his grandma at ten to two. After lunch he relaxes a bit, and at quarter past three he does his homework. At five o’clock he plays football with his friends in the park. He never watches TV in the afternoon! The family has dinner at half past seven. After dinner Leo brushes his teeth, and at five past nine he reads a comic in bed. Finally, he goes to sleep at half past nine.

First page.

CORALINE– Neil Gaiman

“

Coraline discovered the door a little while after they moved into the house.

It was a very old house—it had an attic under the roof and a cellar under the ground and an overgrown garden with huge old trees in it.

Coraline's family didn't own all of the house—it was too big for that. Instead they owned part of it. There were other people who lived in the old house. Miss Spink and Miss Forcible lived in the flat below Coraline's, on the ground floor. They were both old and round, and they lived in their flat with a number of aging Highland terriers. Once upon a time Miss Spink and Miss Forcible had been actresses, as Miss Spink told Coraline the first time she met her. “You see, Caroline,” Miss Spink said, getting Coraline's name wrong, “both myself and Miss Forcible were famous actresses, in our time. We trod the boards, luvvy. Oh, don't let Hamish eat the fruitcake, or he'll be up all night with his tummy.”

“It's Coraline. Not Caroline. Coraline,” said Coraline.

In the flat above Coraline's, under the roof, was a crazy old man with a big mustache. He told Coraline that he was training a mouse circus. He wouldn't let anyone see it.

        3.8 Highlight the intensifiers

        click the words to highlight them

        Alice feels very strange in Chapter 2. She is slightly sad and a bit confused after she falls into Wonderland. When she grows too big, she feels really scared because her arms and legs are extremely long. The room becomes pretty small for her, and she cannot move quite well.

        Then she becomes a little small again, and she feels rather worried because she is not big enough to reach the golden key. The situation is absolutely impossible for her, and she starts to cry so much that she makes a large pool of tears.

        Everything is incredibly strange, but Alice tries to stay calm and think.

        3.9 Highlight the comparisons

        Alice is very curious, she is the most curious character in the book! But the White Rabbit doesn't always answer, he runs away and is faster than Alice.

        The Rabbit is busy, but the Lizard is busier than the Rabbit. He is following his orders!

        Alice drinks a potion and becomes small. She gets smaller and smaller… until she is the smallest creature in the garden! Later, she eats a cake and becomes big. She gets bigger and bigger… until she is the biggest thing in the room!

        After the race, the birds are confused, Alice is more confused than the birds. The Dodo is sure about his decisions. Nobody is surer than he is.

        Yoga poses

        Stretching Up

        Stand with your feet a little apart. // Keep your knees soft, // and your feet steady on the floor. // Now, ~slowly~ reach both arms up high. // Look at something in front of you that isn't moving. // If this feels hard, keep your arms soft and a little bent. // If you want a challenge, // stretch into your fingers, // rise onto your toes, // and gently look up. //

        Forward Bending

        Slide your hands ~slowly~ down your thighs. // Let your knees bend, // and your shoulders relax. // Let your head feel heavy, // and your back stay comfortable. // Bend your knees as much as you need, to feel comfortable. // If you want more, // lengthen your back // and gently reach toward the floor. //

        Tree pose

        ~Stand~ tall on one foot. // Bring your hands together in front of your chest… // or reach them up high, like branches. // Now, place your other foot gently on your ankle, // or on your inner leg — // not on the knee. // Find one still point in front of you, // and look right at it. // Breathe… and hold.

        Warrior pose

        Step your feet wide apart. // Turn your back foot to the side. // Stretch your arms out, // to the sides, // at shoulder height. // Bend your front knee, // so it is above your ankle. // Keep your back leg straight, // and strong. //

        Chair pose

        Bring your feet together, // or a little apart. // Reach your arms up, // in front of you // or by your ears. // Now, bend your knees. // as if you were about to sit in a chair. // Keep your weight on your heels, // and find your balance. //

        HOW TO READ THE SYMBOLS

        = take a slow breath
        // = short pause (1–2 sec)
        ~word~ = say it slowly

        MONEY

        How should money be shared?

        EQUALLY

        "All children get the same pocket money every week, no matter how hard they study or how well they behave."

        BY VALUE

        "Doctors earn more money than painters, because society thinks saving lives is worth more than making art."

        BY HOURS

        "A student who studies 5 hours a day gets more allowance than one who studies 1 hour, even if the second one gets better grades."

        BY NEED

        "A family with 5 children receives more money from the government than a family with 1 child."

        BY RISK TAKEN
        INHERITED

        "If your parents are rich, you get their money and house when they die — even if you never worked a single day."

        DECISIONS

        Who makes the rules?

        ONE LEADER

        "The queen decides everything alone. Nobody can disagree."

        A SMALL
        GROUP OF
        EXPERTS

        "Only the five students with the best grades in science vote on the rules for the science lab."

        EVERYONE

        "Every citizen votes for the President. The person with the most votes wins, even if some people disagree."

        GAP

        How big should the gap between rich and poor be?

        NO GAP

        "Every worker in the factory — from the cleaner to the manager — earns exactly the same salary. You can't inherit money"

        A SMALL GAP
        A BIG GAP

        "The best student in the class can buy all the snacks, wear a crown and sit where they want; students with the worst grades can't afford to eat.

        HELP

        "Everybody pays taxes, the government builds hospitals for everyone."

        RICH PEOPLE
        MUST HELP

        "Rich people pay taxes, the government uses the money to build hospitals for everyone, but rich people can choose to use private doctors. "

        NOBODY

        "Nobody has to help, but sometimes rich people can give charity. They can help only the people they want to help."

        I can… I can't…

        Nova Quick is 13 years old and she lives in Chicago. By day she is a normal student, but when the city needs help, she becomes the fastest girl in the world!

        Nova can run faster than a car and she can jump over a bus. She can see in the dark, too. Her sidekick is Pip, a tiny robot dog. Pip can fly and he can talk, but he can't swim: water breaks him!

        Nova has two weaknesses. First, she can't say no to pizza, and the villains know it. Second, she can't stay awake after 9 pm. “Even superheroes need sleep,” she says.

        7 True or false?

        2. Nova can fly.
        3. Pip is a real dog.

        5. Nova can stay awake all night.
        6. The villains know Nova's weakness.
        8 Answer in a full sentence
        1. What can Pip do?
        2. Why can't Pip swim?
        3. What are Nova's two weaknesses?

        Sports & Hobbies

        Love playing · grammar

        Love, like… hate!

        • ❤️loveI love swimming.
        • 🙂likeShe likes reading.
        • 😐don't mindWe don't mind cleaning.
        • 👎don't likeHe doesn't like running.
        • 💔hateThey hate getting up early.

        After love, like, don't mind, don't like, hate we use the -ing form: I love playing video games.

        With he / she / it: likes, loves, hates and doesn't like. The -ing word never changes!

        + ingplay → playing
        read → reading
        −e + ingdance → dancing
        bake → baking
        double + ingswim → swimming
        run → running

        🧱 Scaffolding · lesson plan

        Sports & Hobbies ⚽

        Four lessons: first can, then love / like / hate + -ing.

        1 Talents GR: can

        • Lead-in: mime sports and the class guesses → Mime it!
        • Two truths, one lie about abilities → Ex. 3
        • Mime chain: one mimes, the next says “she can cook” and mimes something else.
        • Mime charades on the computer (project it): one pupil mimes a card, the class guesses. You choose the levels (easy, medium, hard or a mix), the timer and 1 or 2 teams → the game corner of this page.
        • Production: the superhero with 5 abilities and 2 things they can't do → Nova Quick · Ex. 9
        • Superhero based on you (optional): start from what they really can do, then “×1000” (jump high for volleyball → jump over buildings; good at listening → read people's emotions) → scaffolding lines on this page and the Superpower workshop in its game corner.

        Homework: the book exercises · two truths, one lie about what you can do · a superhero (5 abilities, 2 weaknesses, original!). Optional: a superhero based on you, with your abilities and flaws, named.

        2 Love playing GR: like + -ing

        • Correct the homework (the two truths and one lie).
        • Impostor cards (your set of cards). Homework: translate the words you have → Ex. 21
        • Guess the Person: each pupil writes 5 things (love, like, don't mind, don't like, hate); you collect and read them → Ex. 13–14
        • Perfect Roommate Ad → Ex. 15

        Material: photos of sports and hobbies. Homework: the book exercises · the roommate ad. Optional $100: a short video “promoting” your favorite hobby → videos

        🧱 Scaffolding · lesson plan

        3 Impostor + -ing GR: like + -ing

        • Correct the homework: two truths, one lie.
        • Emoji reaction: show photos of hobbies and sports; the pupils answer 👍 or 👎 → Emoji reaction
        • Guess the Person again, with new papers → Ex. 13–14

        Material: photos of sports and hobbies. Homework: the book exercises. Optional $100: promo video. Optional $80: a short video miming 5 actions you can, can't, like, don't like or don't mind doing; after the video, write the action you were miming → videos

        4 Impostor + -ing GR: like + -ing

        • My Weekend Scale from ❤️ to 💔: “I love reading but I hate ironing.” Elicit. → Ex. 11–12
        • Opinion Line-Up: you say an activity and they stand in a line from “love” to “hate”, then talk to the person at the opposite end: “I like swimming. What about you?” → Move and talk!
        • Perfect Roommate Ad → Ex. 15

        Material: photos of sports and hobbies. Homework: write an ad for the ideal roommate with the appreciation verbs (love, like… hate) and can.

        Grammar

        I am… I feel…

        Use be or feel + a feeling word. I’m happy = I feel happy. Both are OK!

        +I’m happy.She’s happy.
        They’re happy.
        −I’m not sad.He isn’t sad.
        We aren’t sad.
        ?Are you tired?Yes, I am.
        No, I’m not.

        ⚠️ In English we say I’m scared, not “I have fear”. Feelings use be, never have!

        🧱 Scaffolding · lesson plan

        Emotions · how do you feel?

        Level A1+/A2, like the other chapters of the 1st year: be + feeling, feel, because, a little / very / extremely (seen in Alice), -er / more / the most, When I’m …, I …. No past tense, no technical words.

        1 Faces & words 15 feelings

        The cover and faces · Meet the crew

        • Warm-up: pupils click ✓ the feelings they know; match and write the faces (1, 2); read the nine cards aloud (I feel … when …).
        • Body clues (3) and “How do they feel?” (4). Computer: Emotion Wheel as a warm-up or a reward.

        2 Be, feel, because grammar

        I am… I feel… · Mia’s week

        • Rule cards (+ − ?) and the typical mistake I have fear → I’m scared. Exercises 5–9, speaking in pairs.
        • Reading “Mia’s week”: true/false, why? (because), join the halves, the sentence machine.

        3 The body and the size of a feeling vocabulary

        Body talk · Small & BIG feelings

        • Verbs for the body (smile, cry, shout…), the body map, the dialogue in order (drag or type the number).
        • Ladders: drag the words to the steps; intensifiers (they know them from Alice); “My feelings meter”.

        4 Reading and wellbeing CLIL-light

        Four friends · The calm toolkit

        • Chat reading, advice (A/B/C), a reply message. The box-breathing diagram can be done together with the class (1 minute).
        • Match it!, my own toolkit, the calm-down staircase. Computer: Coping Crew (play with the whole class: each team keeps its score).

        4b More coping ideas wellbeing

        5-4-3-2-1 · I-messages · Kind thoughts · control · Crossword · ask for help

        • Ideas of the Coping Library, simplified: grounding with the senses, “I” messages, kind thoughts, what I can / can’t control, asking for help, a 5-minute plan. Pupils rate the strategies (1–5) to find what works for them.
        • Crossword of Coping Crew on paper (11 × 11, word bank under the clues): pair work or homework.

        5 Compare, say it, play speaking

        Compare! · Say it with feeling · Tic-Tac-Toe

        • Compare! table and cards; Sentence dice with a real die (the six faces are printed on the page); Tic-Tac-Toe: two teams, one board each, the other team accepts or rejects the sentence.

        6 My diary and checkpoint review

        My feelings diary · My words & me

        • A week of feelings (draw the face, one word, because). Homework: the words in Italian and the optional poster.

        Neurons and plasticity

        Your brain has about 86 billion . A neuron is a very small cell. It sends messages to other neurons with a little . The place where two neurons meet is called a .

        When you repeat something, the same neurons send messages again and again. The synapse becomes , like a path in a forest: when many people walk on it, the path becomes wide and clear. Scientists say: neurons that fire together, together.

        Our lived in nature and had to learn fast: Which fruit is good? Where is the river? Their brains changed every day because they practiced every day. In London, taxi drivers learn 25,000 streets, and the (the part of the brain for memory) becomes bigger in them. The brain can change: this is called .

        For my lessonOne explanation is not enough. Give your class time to practice, again and again!

        Lab 2 · Learn & check

        The small desk

        🎲Play›📖Learn & check
        11 Put the paragraphs in order the text about chunks is mixed up

        On the computer: drag a paragraph by its letter, or press ▲ ▼. On paper: write 1 to 5 in the boxes.

        1. ABut the brain has a clever trick: it makes groups. A group is called a chunk. For example, the letters F, B and I are three letters, but you know them together, so they are only one chunk.
        2. BChunks help you with phone numbers, songs and long words too. Remember: if the desk is full, new information falls off. So a good teacher gives you a few chunks, not a long list.
        3. CImagine you are a hunter, 100,000 years ago. In the savanna you must watch the animals, the weather and your friends. But your brain cannot keep everything in mind. It has a small desk for the information that you use now. Scientists call this desk working memory.
        4. DThe hunter does the same. He does not see a lot of different animals: he sees three chunks, “danger”, “food” and “friends”. In this way there is always a free place on his desk.
        5. EThe desk is very small. In 1956 a scientist, George Miller, thought that it has about seven places. Today scientists think that it has only about four. For the hunter this is a problem: a lion, a river, a friend and a storm are already four things!
        For my lessonTeach only 3 or 4 new words, never 10. Put them in a group: same topic, same picture, same story.

        Lab 3 · Learn & check

        Why do we forget?

        🎲Play›📖Learn & check
        17 Put the paragraphs back choose A, B, C or D for each gap

        The forgetting curve

        In 1885 Hermann Ebbinghaus wants to measure memory. He invents words with no meaning, like DAX and ZOL, because real words are already connected to other memories.

        1

        The loss is fast at the beginning and then slow: this is the forgetting curve. Forgetting is not a mistake of the brain. The brain uses 20% of the energy of your body, so it cannot keep everything.

        2

        Ebbinghaus also looks for a solution to forgetting.

        3

        Today we know that this method, called review, is the best way to remember for a long time.

        A He learns a list and tests himself after twenty minutes. He forgets almost half of the words. After one day he forgets more than half.

        B He studies the list again after one day and after one week. This time he forgets much less.

        C It keeps what is important or what you use often, and it throws away the rest. For our ancestors the place of a lion was important. The color of a leaf was not.

        D He eats a big breakfast and the words stay in his head forever.

        18 True or false? a small check
        1. Ebbinghaus invents words with no meaning.
        2. The brain keeps everything.
        3. Review helps you remember for a long time.

        Lab 4 · Learn & check

        Play is practice

        🎲Play›📖Learn & check

        Why do animals play?

        Watch a young lion, a puppy or a monkey: they run, jump, hide and fight for fun. Why do animals play? Scientists think that play is practice for adult life. A young lion that plays at hunting makes mistakes without danger.

        Humans are the most playful animals. When children play, their brains make millions of new connections. When you do something yourself, your brain works more than when you only listen. The scientist Robert Sapolsky watched baboons in Kenya for more than thirty years. For him, friends and games are very important in animal life.

        Key words · write the Italian

        Lab 5 · Learn & check

        The zebra and the lion

        🎲Play›📖Learn & check

        Emotions and memory

        A zebra drinks at a river. Suddenly it sees a lion! In the zebra's brain, a small part called the amygdala sends an alarm: the heart beats faster and the muscles are ready to run. At the same time, the hippocampus keeps the memory: “Danger! This place is not safe.”

        A zebra that forgets the lion does not live long. So evolution made emotional memories very strong. You remember your first day of school or an embarrassing moment, but not what you ate on a normal Tuesday. A little stress helps memory. Robert Sapolsky says: zebras do not get stomach ulcers, because when the lion goes away, they relax. Humans can worry for weeks.

        32 Choose the answer A, B or C
        1. What does the amygdala do when the zebra sees the lion?
          AIt sends an alarm.BIt eats.CIt sleeps.
        2. Why are emotional memories strong?
          AThey help us to survive.BThey are boring.CThey are very short.
        3. Why do zebras not get ulcers?
          AThey do not drink.BThey relax when the lion goes away.CThey are very strong.

        Lab 6 · Learn & check

        An expensive organ

        🎲Play›📖Learn & check

        Attention and cognitive load

        Your brain is only 2% of your body weight, but it uses about 20% of your energy! For our ancestors food was not easy to find, so the brain was careful with energy. That is why attention is small: you can watch only a few things at the same time.

        If you do two difficult things, for example listen to a teacher and write a message, your brain changes from one to the other and makes mistakes. Scientists call this work cognitive load. Too much information overloads the brain, and it forgets.

        🧱 Scaffolding · lesson plan

        Teach Teaching 🧠

        Like a science book: play (the pupils try, notice, say the rule), learn (a short text about the brain and evolution, written in simple English), check (a different kind of exercise in every lab).

        ★ Opening Cover

        • The cover, then Wire your brain with the brain words to translate (Italian).

        Homework: the brain words in Italian.

        1 Neurons Check: cloze

        • Lesson A · play → neuron counter, the wire experiment (let them press, don't explain), the hippocampus vote → Wire your brain, Can a brain grow?
        • Lesson B · learn & check (can be homework) → the text “Your brain is a forest”: the blue words are the gaps of a cloze, with a word bank → Learn & check

        2 Chunks Check: put the sentences in order

        • Lesson A · play → letter test: round 1, then round 2 without saying that the letters are the same; scores on the board → The letter test, The magic number
        • Lesson B · learn & check (can be homework) → “The small desk”: a text about chunks cut into five paragraphs to put in order (drag them on the screen, numbers on paper) → Learn & check

        3 Forgetting Check: put the paragraphs back

        • Lesson A · play → sliders first, reveal after; the “Tomorrow” box is for the first 3 minutes of the next lesson → The forgetting curve, Review wins!
        • Lesson B · learn & check (can be homework) → “Why do we forget?” and a text with three missing paragraphs (A–D, one is extra) → Learn & check

        🧱 Scaffolding · lesson plan

        4 Active learning Check: true or false and correct

        • Lesson A · play → swimming, active or passive, then the pair experiment (15 minutes, a timer; count the green boxes: 10 words per list, nobody remembers all) → Do it!, Teach to learn
        • Lesson B · learn & check (can be homework) → “Play is practice” (young animals, the baboons of Sapolsky) → Learn & check. They correct the false sentences in writing.

        5 Emotions Check: multiple choice

        • Lesson A · play → the two neighbors, the “proof” in pairs, rate the hooks → Feel it, keep it, Rate the hooks
        • Lesson B · learn & check (can be homework) → “The zebra and the lion” (amygdala, hippocampus, stress) → Learn & check

        6 Cognitive load Check: join the halves

        • Lesson A · play → the full glass, chaos or organized, sort the dolphin facts → The full glass, Organize the chaos
        • Lesson B · learn & check (can be homework) → “An expensive organ” (the brain uses 20% of the energy) → Learn & check

        7 The Teaching Menu Induction → menu

        • The volleyball lesson: label the 4 parts, find the pattern, match with the labs, tell it with first, then, after, finally → pages. They discover the four parts before they see the menu.
        • The menu → 1 · 2, 3 · 4. Each part says choose ONE. Make the groups (3–4 pupils): each group chooses a different topic.

        Homework: think of 2 topics and bring one object or picture.

        Metaphors

        A figure of speech that describes an object by comparing it to another object with similar characteristics.

        A · the real thingYour smileISB · the imagesunshineWhat do they have in common?bright · warm · they make people happy

        SIMILE one thing is LIKE another (like / as)You are sly as a fox. 🦊

        METAPHOR one thing IS anotherYour lips are cherries. 🍒

        The 4 rules of metaphors

        1. 1NOT to be taken literallyp. →
        2. 2They CANNOT be reversedp. →
        3. 3We can’t help but consider the literal meaningp. →
        4. 4We can’t ignore the metaphorical meaning eitherp. →

        Rule 1 of 4

        NOT to be taken literally

        ✏️ Disegno

        “It’s raining cats and dogs!” = It’s raining very, very hard. No animals are falling from the sky! A metaphor is an image, not a fact.

        Rule 4 of 4

        But we can’t ignore the metaphorical meaning either

        ✏️ Disegno

        🔬 The experiment

        1. People read sentences and say as fast as possible: is it literally true or false?
        2. Some sentences are simply false: “A cat is a car.” Others are metaphors: “My teacher is a dragon.” Literally, they are false too!
        3. Saying “false” to a metaphor takes longer: the brain understands the metaphorical meaning anyway, and it gets in the way.
        4. Stroke patients had much bigger difficulties recognizing metaphors as not literally true.

        stroke = ictus · literally = alla lettera

        5.2 Detective 🔎 Simile, metaphor or just a fact?
        1. Her eyes are lamps in the dark.
        2. His voice is like thunder.
        3. He has a long scar on his arm.
        4. My hands are ice.
        5. Her cheeks are as red as tomatoes.
        6. She is as tall as her brother.
        7. His heart is a locked door.
        8. Her laugh sounds like a bell.
        9. She has the same nose as her mother.
        10. My feet are two tired boats.

        Careful! like and as are not always a simile. If you compare two real things of the same kind (two people, two noses), it’s just a fact: there is no image.

        The Big 5

        describing personality

        Scientists studied thousands of people and discovered something interesting: we can describe ALL personalities using just 5 big categories. We call them THE BIG 5, or OCEAN.

        1. OOPENNESSopen to new things
        2. CCONSCIENTIOUSNESSresponsible and organized
        3. EEXTRAVERSIONloves hanging out with people
        4. AAGREEABLENESSgenerous and avoids fights
        5. NNEUROTICISManxious

          10.3 Read the file of a villain 🔍

          NAMEPaola Theprofessor

          Name and surnamePaola Fatigato

          Description The Prof has a very long chin and she is short (too short to play attack in volleyball, but she tried anyway). She has frizzy hair that she braids into small braids. She thinks she is better than everyone. She has 5 university degrees and she is always right. She talks a lot and she is not very precise, and she considers herself a bookworm, but she is proud of who she is! Her confidence is her power.

          History One day, she was skateboarding to school very fast. She was talking on the phone and not paying attention. She crashed into a science laboratory truck. Strange chemicals fell on her and she got superpowers!

          Main
          attack

          “The Endless Talk” – Paola talks and talks and talks. Enemies get tired and confused.

          Equipment

          • Skateboard.
          • The Big Book: Contains all the facts.
          • Microphone Earrings: Make her focus on the sounds she wants to hear and ignore the rest.
          • Rainbow pens: Organized in chromatic order. They can correct every mistake.

          Powers

          – Ego Shield: A shield made of pure confidence. It stops attacks, especially offenses.
          – Instant Expert: She can become an expert in anything in 5 seconds. She reads one page and knows everything.

          Weaknesses

          She needs to be fed or she cannot use her powers.
          She falls asleep at 22:22 whatever she is doing.

          Goals
          Teach everyone everything she knows
          Create students who can make a better world

          Sidekicks
          The Boyfriend: He feeds her and her ego. He tells her she is amazing, but he also tells her when she is wrong.
          The Best Friend: No matter how long Paola talks, she is always there.

          The rules

          What is a sonnet?

          • ✦14 lines: 3 quatrains (4 lines) + 1 couplet (2 lines)
          • ◐10 syllables in every line
          • ☾iambic pentameter: da-DUM da-DUM da-DUM da-DUM da-DUM, like a heartbeat
          • ✧rhyme scheme: ABAB CDCD EFEF GG
          • ↺the couplet (the last 2 lines) is the twist: it changes everything!

          Romeo & Juliet
          Act I · Scene I

          The fight

          Verona, a street. Two servants of the Capulets meet a servant of the Montagues…

          My role:click your character: your lines light up

          Sampson: Gregory, we will not carry insults. If a Montague looks at us, we fight.

          Gregory: Yes, but let them start first.

          (Enter Abram.)

          Sampson: Do you bite your thumb at us, sir?

          Abram: I bite my thumb.

          Sampson: Do you bite your thumb at us?

          Abram: No… I just bite my thumb.

          Gregory: Do you want a fight?

          Abram: If you want one.

          (They draw swords. Enter Benvolio.)

          Benvolio: Stop! Put your swords away. You do not know what you are doing! Make peace!

          (Enter Tybalt.)

          Tybalt: What? Drawn swords and talk of peace? I hate the word “peace.” I hate it as I hate hell, all Montagues, and you!

          (They fight.)

          Benvolio: I try to keep peace!

          Tybalt: And I try to fight!

          Script

          The kiss

          My role:click your character: your lines light up

          Romeo: If I have touched your hand in a wrong way, let me fix it with a gentle kiss. My lips are like two pilgrims, ready to show respect to this holy place.

          Juliet: Good pilgrim, you are too hard on yourself. Pilgrims may touch hands with saints. Palm to palm is a holy kiss.

          Romeo: Do not saints also have lips?

          Juliet: Yes, but they use them to pray.

          Romeo: Then let our lips pray together.

          Juliet: Saints do not move… but they listen.

          Romeo: Then do not move while I take my prayer.

          (He kisses her.)

          Juliet: O Romeo, Romeo! Wherefore art thou Romeo?
          Deny thy father and refuse thy name.
          ’Tis but thy name that is my enemy.
          What’s in a name? That which we call a rose
          By any other word would smell as sweet.
          Juliet: How camest thou hither, tell me, and wherefore?
          The orchard walls are high and hard to climb,
          And the place death, considering who thou art,
          If any of my kinsmen find thee here.
          Romeo: With love's light wings did I o'erperch these walls,
          For stony limits cannot hold love out;
          And what love can do, that dares love attempt.

          Script

          The balcony

          My role:click your character: your lines light up

          Juliet: Oh Romeo, Romeo… why must you be Romeo? Leave your family name, and I will no longer be a Capulet. It is only your name that is my enemy. A rose would smell sweet even if we called it something else.

          Romeo: (whispering) Should I stay quiet… or speak?

          Juliet: Who is there? Who are you, hiding in the dark? Why do you listen to my secret thoughts?

          Romeo: I do not know how to tell you my name. My name is my enemy, because you do not like it.

          Juliet: I have not heard many words, but I know your voice. You are Romeo, aren't you?

          Romeo: Yes… my name is Romeo. But I would change it for you.

          Juliet: If my family sees you, they will kill you.

          Romeo: Love helped me climb these walls. Stone walls cannot stop true love. Nothing can!

          Clothes & Fashion show
          ENGLISH · FASHION SHOW

          Organizing our fashion show

          We will have it before Christmas. Everybody will be involved!

          roles

          Every role has its own tasks and its own grade.

          Models

          Walk the runway wearing outfits and show confidence. 1 Pick from a list of necessary clothes. 2 You can exchange them with the other models. 3 Send me pictures of the outfits and descriptions.

          You will be graded for

          • the description of your outfit
          • originality
          • confidence and performance in the show

          Assistants

          Help the models dress and organize the clothes backstage. You will be in charge of three or four models.

          You will be graded for

          • the description of one outfit of your models
          • the backstage organization
          • the tidiness of the space at the end of the event

          Hosts & commentators

          Describe each outfit’s color, style and materials clearly. You can read from a script, but you must speak only in English. Each host describes at least 2 models.

          You will be graded for

          • fluency
          • pronunciation
          • performance

          Judges

          Watch carefully and score creativity, style and presentation. You will have an evaluation sheet to complete (p. ). At the end of the show, you will announce the winners in several categories.

          You will be graded for

          • the explanation of the criteria that guided your choices

          Photographers

          Show + photoshoot. You will bring a camera on the day of the show.

          You will be graded for

          • the quality of your 5 best pictures (your choice)
          • the description of 1 picture (teacher’s choice)
          • the originality of the poses and compositions

          Makeup artists

          Print the makeups you intend on recreating. Make a deal with at least three models who want their makeup done by you.

          You will be graded for

          • your best makeup (originality and execution)
          • the description of one random makeup
          • the description of one model’s outfit (your choice)
          • the use of makeup-related vocabulary

          Hair stylists

          Braids, ponytails, styles with gel or accessories. You cannot wash, cut or use straighteners. Make a deal with at least three models.

          You will be graded for

          • your best hairstyle (originality and execution)
          • the description of one random hairstyle
          • the description of one model’s outfit (your choice)
          • the use of hairstyling vocabulary

          Case files · prepositions of place

          Murdoku

          murder + sudoku:
          find the murderer!

          1. 1The map is a grid of squares. Thick lines divide it into rooms.
          2. 2Everybody is in one square. In every row and every column there is exactly ONE person.
          3. 3Nobody can be in a hatched square (plants, mirrors, boxes…). You can be on a chair, a sofa, a bed or a rug, in a bathtub, under a table.
          4. 4The victim is in a room with ONE other person: the murderer!
          • in the kitchena square of that room
          • on a chairthe square of the chair
          • under the tablethe square of the table
          • next to the planta square that touches it ← → ↑ ↓ (not diagonal)
          • between A and BA on one side, B on the other side
          • in front of the TVthe square the TV looks at
          1 Case 1 · Backstage
          ★☆☆

          The fashion show starts in ten minutes, but Coco, the star model, is dead! Tap a name, then tap a square. Use ✗ for “nobody here”.

                          ⚠️ Watch out!

                          on = touching it · above = higher up, NOT touching

                          under = covered by it · below = lower down

                          in front of = right before it · opposite = face to face, on the other side

                          0.1 My summer book

                          Task 1 · the script

                          My book review

                          Write the four parts in this order. Look at the model book review on p. for ideas!

                          1 · Summary what happens · 6–8 sentences · present simple

                          • Who is the main character? Where and when is the story set?
                          • What is the problem? What happens?
                          • How does it end? (in a review you can keep the ending a secret!)
                          The story is set in…The main character is…At the beginning…One day…Then… / After that…In the end…

                          2 · Personal comment your opinion · 6–8 sentences

                          • Did you like it? Why or why not?
                          • What is your favorite part or character? What didn't you like?
                          • How did the book make you feel? What did you learn?
                          I really enjoyed it because…My favorite part is when…It made me feel…However, I didn't like…I learned that…

                          3 · Recommendation who should read it? · 2–3 sentences

                          • Who would enjoy this book? How many stars do you give it? ★★★★★
                          I recommend this book to…It's perfect for readers who…If you liked…, you will love…I give it … stars because…

                          4 · Character sheet at least 2 characters · 3–4 sentences each

                          • Name and role: protagonist, antagonist or secondary character?
                          • What does he / she look like? What is he / she like (personality)?
                          • What does he / she want? What does he / she do in the story? Draw them if you like!
                          He / She is…He / She has got…He / She wants to…He / She is the protagonist / antagonist.

                          ✍️ Write it by hand in your notebook or on a sheet of paper. Don't translate from Italian sentence by sentence: use the phrases!

                          Summer holidays

                          Task 2 · open it in 5 years!

                          Dear future me…

                          Write a letter to the person you will be in 5 years. Tell them about this summer: what do you want to remember?

                          1. Start: Dear future me, / Hi, future (your name)!
                          2. Now: how old you are, where you are, what you like at the moment.
                          3. This summer (past simple!): places, people, the best moments, something funny, something new.
                          4. Remember: the things you never want to forget, a song, a smell, a feeling.
                          5. Questions and wishes for your future self, then end: Love, / See you in the future, + your name.
                          This summer I went…Do you remember when…?Don't forget…I hope you still…Are you still friends with…?I will never forget…
                          MODEL

                          Dear future me,

                          I'm 13 and I'm writing from my grandma's garden in Puglia. This summer I learned to swim underwater and I ate the best watermelon of my life! In July we went camping with my cousins: it rained every night, but we laughed a lot. Please remember the smell of the sea in the morning and the song we sang in the car. Do you still play the guitar? I hope you are happy and still kind to everyone.

                          See you in the future, Sara

                          0.2 Before you write: my summer memories

                          Task 3 · you'll be so proud

                          Dear past me…

                          Write to the person you were a year ago. Tell them about one episode from this summer: why would they be proud of you?

                          1. Start: Dear past me, / Hi, little (your name)!
                          2. Set the scene: when was it? Where were you? Who were you with?
                          3. Tell the story in order (past simple!): first, then, after that, suddenly, in the end.
                          4. Why it's important: how did you feel? Why would your past self be proud of you?
                          5. A piece of advice for your past self, then end: With love, / Your future self.
                          You won't believe it, but…Last summer I…At first I was scared, but…Suddenly…In the end I…You will be proud because…Don't worry about…
                          MODEL

                          Dear past me,

                          You won't believe it, but this summer I jumped from a rock into the sea! It was August and I was with my friends in Sardinia. First I looked down and my legs were shaking. My friends jumped, but I waited for ten minutes. Then I closed my eyes, counted to three and… splash! The water was cold and I screamed, but I was so happy. You were always scared of deep water, so I know you are proud of me. Don't worry: one day you will be brave too.

                          With love, your future self, Luca

                          0.6 Regular verbs: the spelling rules

                          most verbs: + edvisit → visited · play → played · enjoy → enjoyed

                          verb ends in -e: + ddance → danced · arrive → arrived

                          consonant + y → iedtry → tried · study → studied
                          (but vowel + y: stay → stayed)

                          1 vowel + 1 consonant: double itstop → stopped · travel → traveled

                          Test C · Summer homework

                          First page.

                          THE BOY WHO HARNESSED THE WIND– William Kamkwamba & Bryan Mealer

                          “

                          Before I discovered the miracles of science, magic ruled the world.

                          Magic and its many mysteries were a presence that hovered about constantly, giving me my earliest memory as a boy—the time my father saved me from certain death and became the hero he is today.

                          I was six years old, playing in the road, when a group of herd boys approached, singing and dancing. This was in Masitala village near the city of Kasungu, where my family lived on a farm. They explained how they’d been tending their herd that morning and discovered a giant sack in the road. When they opened it up, they found it filled with bubble gum. I can’t tell you how much I loved bubble gum.

                          “Should we give some to this boy?” one asked.

                          I didn’t move or breathe. There were dead leaves in my hair.

                          “Eh, why not?” said another. “Just look at him.”

                          One of the boys reached into the bag and pulled out a handful of gumballs, one for every color, and dropped them into my hands. As the boys left, I felt the sweet juice roll down my chin and soak my shirt.

                          ⏸ Stop 1 Missing sentences

                          Three sentences are missing from the text. Write the right letter in each gap 1–3. There is one extra sentence you do not need!

                          • AI put them in my pocket for later.
                          • BCan you imagine such a treasure?
                          • CI stuffed them all in my mouth.
                          • DThe herd boys worked for a nearby farmer who kept many cows.
                          📌 Grammar Past simple: find the verbs in the text

                          The story is in the past simple: “they found it filled with bubble gum”. Regular verbs + -ed (drop → dropped!), irregular verbs change. Write the past.

                          1. find →
                          2. feel →
                          3. leave →
                          4. say →
                          5. drop →
                          6. pull →
                          🔮 Guess! The next day, a man on a bicycle arrives. Who is he?
                          1. I think he is…

                          The following day, I was playing under the mango tree when a trader on a bicycle stopped to chat with my father. He said that while on his way to the market the previous morning, he’d dropped one of his bags. By the time he’d realized what had happened and circled back, someone had taken it. The bag was filled with bubble gum, he said. Some fellow traders had told him about the herd boys passing out gum in the villages, and this made him very angry. For two days he’d been riding his bicycle throughout the district looking for the boys. He then issued a chilling threat.

                          “I’ve gone to see the sing’anga, and whoever ate that gum will soon be sorry.”

                          🔮 Guess! What will William do now?
                          1. William is scared. He…

                          I’d swallowed the gum long before. Now the sweet, lingering memory of it soured into poison on my tongue. Without anyone seeing, I ran into the blue gum grove behind my house, leaned against a tree, and tried to make myself clean. I spit and hocked, shoved my finger into my throat, anything to rid my body of the curse. I came up dry. A bit of saliva colored the leaves at my feet, so I covered them with dirt.

                          But then, as if a dark cloud had passed over the sun, I felt the great eye of the wizard watching me through the trees. That night, the witches would come for me in my bed. They’d take me aboard their planes and force me to fight, leaving me for dead along the magic battlefields. And as my soul drifted alone and forsaken above the clouds, my body would be cold by morning. A fear of death swept over me like a fever.

                          I began crying so hard I couldn’t move my legs. The tears ran hot down my face, and as they did, the smell of poison filled my nose. It was everywhere inside me. I fled the forest as fast as possible, trying to get away from the giant magic eye. I ran all the way home to where my father sat against the house, plucking a pile of maize. I wanted to throw my body under his, so he could protect me from the devil.

He told the man what had happened, about the herd boys coming by and giving me the stolen gum. Then without question, my father paid the man for his entire bag, which amounted to a full week’s pay.

                          That evening after supper, my life having been saved, I asked my father about the curse, and if he’d truly believed I was finished. He straightened his face and became very serious.

                          “Oh yes, we were just in time,” he said, then started laughing in that way that made me so happy, his big chest heaving and causing the wooden chair to squeal. “William, who knows what was in store for you?”

                          9.13 The forehead game: how to play
                          1. Your teacher gives you a job card. Don't look at it!
                          2. Put it on your forehead (a headband or some tape helps).
                          3. Walk around the class. Ask one yes/no question to a classmate, then change partner.
                          4. Your classmates read your card and answer: Yes / No / Sometimes.
                          5. Do you know? Ask: “Am I a vet?” Right? Take a new card! 🎉

                          Asking about yourself

                          action, routineDo I + verb…?Do I work outside? → Yes, you do. / No, you don't.

                          how I amAm I + adjective…?Am I famous? → Yes, you are. / No, you aren't.

                          the final guessAm I a / an + job?Am I an astronaut? → Yes, you are! 🎉

                          9.19 Read about these real jobs
                          1. 🍦

                            ice-cream taster

                            They taste new ice-cream flavors and decide if they are good. They use a golden spoon, and one taster's tongue was insured for one million dollars!

                          2. 🌪️

                            storm chaser

                            They drive after tornadoes and big storms to film them and study them. They travel thousands of kilometers. It's exciting, but it can be dangerous!

                          3. 🎮

                            video game tester

                            They play new video games before they come out, look for bugs (mistakes) and write reports. Sometimes they play the same level a hundred times!

                          4. 🐼

                            panda keeper

                            In China, panda keepers look after baby pandas. They feed them, wash them and play with them… and they clean a lot of panda poo!

                          5. 🎬

                            stunt performer

                            They do the dangerous scenes in films instead of the actors: they fall, fight, jump and crash cars. They have to train a lot and be very careful.

                          6. 🛏️

                            bed tester

                            They sleep in new beds and hotels, and tell the company if the beds are comfortable. Yes, they get paid to sleep! They write a report every morning.

                                🎲 My job card: a car mechanic

                                A car mechanic is someone who repairs cars. They work inside, in a garage, but sometimes they have to go outside to help people when their car breaks down on the road. They usually work in the day, from Monday to Friday, and sometimes on Saturday morning. They make quite a lot of money, but they aren't rich. They work with customers and with a small team. They use a lot of tools, for example a wrench and a screwdriver, and they wear a blue uniform. A mechanic has to be strong, patient and good with their hands. They also have to be good with computers, because modern cars are very complicated. The good side is that you can help people and you never get bored. The bad side is that you have to work in a dirty and noisy place.

                                🌟 The job of my dreams: a soccer player

                                I dream of becoming a professional soccer player. I started playing soccer when I was six, and now I play for a team in my town. I would like to play for a big team, like Inter or Juventus, and one day for the national team.

                                I think it is the job of my dreams for many reasons. A soccer player works outside, on the field, and inside, in the gym, but they rarely sit at a desk and study, and I don't enjoy studying very much. You get to work with a team, you can travel all over the world, you can become famous and you make a lot of money. But it isn't an easy job: you have to train every day, you have to eat healthy food and you have to go to bed early. You also have to play on the weekend, so you don't have a lot of free time for your family. I think I can accept these things because I love playing, and I already train three times a week. Maybe living far from my family could be a problem, but I can call them every day and they can come and watch my games. I think I am a good team player, I am physically fit and I am brave. I need to work on my patience, because sometimes I get angry when we lose. It's the perfect job for me because I love sports, and friends and teamwork are very important to me. I want to work hard to make my dream come true!

                                5. Right? One point for the team! 🎉

                                2 Pick a job card and describe the job

                                🎲 My job card: a car mechanic

                                Write 8–10 sentences.

                                A car mechanic is someone who repairs cars. They work inside, in a garage, but sometimes they have to go outside to help people when their car breaks down on the road. They usually work in the day, from Monday to Friday, and sometimes on Saturday morning. They make quite a lot of money, but they aren't rich. They work with customers and with a small team. They use a lot of tools, for example a wrench and a screwdriver, and they wear a blue uniform. A mechanic has to be strong, patient and good with their hands. They also have to be good with computers, because modern cars are very complicated. The good side is that you can help people and you never get bored. The bad side is that you have to work in a dirty and noisy place.

                                3 The job of my dreams

                                Write a text of at least 100 words. Use would like to, want to, dream of and can / have to.

                                I dream of becoming a professional soccer player. I started playing soccer when I was six, and now I play for a team in my town. I would like to play for a big team, like Inter or Juventus, and one day for the national team.

                                I think it is the job of my dreams for many reasons. A soccer player works outside, on the field, and inside, in the gym, but they rarely sit at a desk and study, and I don't enjoy studying very much. You get to work with a team, you can travel all over the world, you can become famous and you make a lot of money. But it isn't an easy job: you have to train every day, you have to eat healthy food and you have to go to bed early. You also have to play on the weekend, so you don't have a lot of free time for your family. I think I can accept these things because I love playing, and I already train three times a week. Maybe living far from my family could be a problem, but I can call them every day and they can come and watch my games. I think I am a good team player, I am physically fit and I am brave. I need to work on my patience, because sometimes I get angry when we lose. It's the perfect job for me because I love sports, and friends and teamwork are very important to me. I want to work hard to make my dream come true!

                                Writinga CV

                                your life, your studies, your skills… in one page!

                                What is a CV? A CV (curriculum vitae, Latin for “the course of your life”) is a short document about you: your studies, your experience and your skills. You send it when you look for a job, an internship or a summer job. In the USA it is called a résumé.

                                Literature · 09

                                Meet theAuthor

                                WHO WAS I?

                                a famous writer…
                                but who?

                                Your teacher is a famous writer from the past. But who was he? Work in teams of detectives: study the clues, make inferences and check them with yes / no questions. Every YES is a fact. The team with the most facts wins!

                                9.1 How to play
                                1. Each team asks one question per turn.
                                2. The author answers only YES or NO.
                                3. A grammar mistake? No answer: you lose your turn!
                                4. Every YES = 1 fact = 1 point. Write it on p. .
                                5. Guess his name: +5 points!

                                Our team

                                9.2 Yes / no questions in the past

                                Past simple · every verb

                                Did + subject + base verb…?Did you live in a big city?Yes, I did. / No, I didn’t.

                                Verb to be

                                Was / Were + subject…?Were you rich?Yes, I was. / No, I wasn’t.

                                Past continuous · an action in progress

                                Was / Were + subject + -ing…?Were you working in 1930?Yes, I was. / No, I wasn’t.

                                Did you lived…? Did you live…?Did you were…? Were you…?You were born in Italy? Were you born…?

                                9.3 Think like a detective: from general to specific

                                Did you have a job?YES? →Did you work with people?YES? →Were you a doctor?

                                Topicsfamilyplacesschooljobsmoneyhabitshealthbooks

                                A

                                Paris, March 1945

                                Dear Eileen,

                                Paris is beautiful in spring. These old streets remind me of the years when I was a policeman in France. The coffee here is terrible, but I don’t miss English tea: I never liked it! I’m writing a little book about the animals on a farm. In my story the horses are the leaders. Give a big kiss to our little girl.

                                All my love,
                                George

                                B

                                Jura, Scotland, autumn 1947

                                Dear Jack,

                                I’m writing to you from my house on a small, wild island. It rains every day, like in Burma when I was a young policeman there! I’m working on a new novel about a terrible future. My son Richard is three now: he loves the animals on our farm. My lungs are bad and I smoke too much. Please send me some good strong tea!

                                Best wishes,
                                George

                                Animal Farm · active study

                                Main themes

                                9.23 Who? When? Find an example in the book

                                Deception

                                Hiding the truth and changing reality to trick people.

                                Propaganda

                                Controlling information and using words to control what people think.

                                Idealism

                                The dream of a perfect world, based on high moral values.

                                Exploitation & inequality

                                Using people for your advantage, taking away their rights; different rules and privileges for different people.

                                Apathy

                                No interest: staying passive when you see injustice.

                                Religion

                                Beliefs that distract from real problems, promise future happiness and justify suffering now.

                                Literature · 09 · Part III

                                1984

                                BIG BROTHER IS WATCHING YOU

                                Nineteen Eighty-Four · George Orwell · 1949

                                London, 1984. Britain is now called Airstrip One, a part of the super-state Oceania. The Party controls everything: what people do, what they say, even what they think. Winston Smith works at the Ministry of Truth. His job? Changing the past.

                                9.24 Key words · find them in your book
                                1. 01

                                  Big BrotherThe leader of the Party. Nobody knows if he really exists.

                                  Part 1 · Ch. 1p.
                                2. 02

                                  telescreenA screen in every home: it watches you and listens to you.

                                  Part 1 · Ch. 1p.
                                3. 03

                                  Thought PoliceThey arrest people for what they think.

                                  Part 1 · Ch. 1p.
                                4. 04

                                  Two Minutes HateEvery day, people scream at the enemy on a screen.

                                  Part 1 · Ch. 1p.
                                5. 05

                                  doublethinkBelieving two opposite things at the same time.

                                  Part 1 · Ch. 3p.
                                6. 06

                                  Ministry of TruthWhere Winston works: he changes old newspapers.

                                  Part 1 · Ch. 4p.
                                7. 07

                                  NewspeakThe new language: fewer words, so fewer thoughts.

                                1.1 Lead-in: talk with a partner
                                • What is a fortune teller?
                                • Do you think that fortune tellers can really predict the future?
                                • What star sign are you? What does it say about your personality?

                                This is Mabel, the worst fortune teller in the world! Her predictions are nearly always wrong. Let's take a look at what she's predicted for 2027:

                                • ♈ AriesYou'll have an interesting year. You'll make a new friend at school. They'll be very friendly and kind and have purple hair.
                                • ♉ TaurusYou'll have a very exciting year. You'll travel somewhere new – maybe even a new country. You'll go somewhere on the train. You'll take a lot of photos to remember your adventure.
                                • ♊ GeminiYou'll have a fantastic year. You'll score the winning goal at a football match. You'll discover your new favorite food. You'll climb a tree.
                                • ♋ CancerYou won't have an easy year in 2027. You'll have an exam that'll be the hardest exam ever. You'll lose some money on the bus. You'll eat some chocolate and feel sick. You won't have good weather on your birthday.
                                • ♌ LeoYou'll have a good year. You'll get a new pair of boots. You'll get a new coat. You'll get a new bag. You'll lose your phone. Your parents won't be happy about that!
                                • ♍ VirgoYou'll make an important decision in August 2027. You'll decide to do the right thing. Will it be easy? No, it won't! You'll also get a new pet. It'll be a pet fish.
                                • ♎ LibraYou'll have a good year and a bad year. You won't get the birthday present you want. However, you'll have a great party and do lots of dancing.
                                • ♏ ScorpioYou'll have fun in 2027. You'll watch a film that will make you laugh. You won't have any problems with your friends. You'll invent a new dance that'll make you famous.
                                • ♐ SagittariusYou'll have a very unusual year in 2027. You'll see a dog that can fly. You'll see a tree upside down. You'll see a cat smile.
                                • ♑ CapricornYou'll help lots of people in 2027. You'll help your friend with their homework. You'll help a new person in your class. You'll even help someone in the supermarket!
                                • ♒ AquariusYou won't have a difficult year. You'll sleep a lot. You'll eat a lot of ice cream. You'll watch your favorite film five times.
                                • ♓ PiscesYou'll have a very active year. You'll go swimming in cold water. You'll play tennis three times a week. Will you have fun? Yes, you will!

                                · 1.4 Analysis look at the sentences

                                1. “You won't have an easy year in 2027.”
                                2. “You'll invent a new dance that'll make you famous.”

                                6. How is will contracted?
                                7. How is will not contracted?
                                8. Is the form the same for I, you, he, she, it, we and they?

                                ✅ Affirmative

                                subject + will + base verb

                                I'll travel. She will travel.

                                ❓ Question

                                (question word) + will + subject + base verb

                                Will you travel? Where will you go?

                                ❌ Negative

                                subject + won't + base verb

                                They won't travel.

                                💬 Short answer

                                Yes, + subject + will · No, + subject + won't

                                Yes, I will. No, I won't.
